title: All causally separable quantum processes are quantum circuits with classical control of causal order
authors: Julian Wechs, Alastair A. Abbott, Cyril Branciard
abstract: The concept of causal (non)separability describes whether the causal order between parties that perform local quantum operations is well-defined or indefinite. Causal (non)separability in the general multipartite setting was introduced and studied in [Oreshkov and Giarmatzi, New J. Phys. 18, 093020 (2016); Wechs, Abbott, and Branciard, New J. Phys. 21, 013027 (2019)]. We resolve an open problem from these earlier works by showing -- using a novel "coherent teleportation technique" -- that a sufficient condition for causal separability identified in [Wechs, Abbott, and Branciard, New J. Phys. 21, 013027 (2019)] is also necessary, and thus provides a complete characterisation of multipartite causal separability. A consequence of this result is that all causally separable processes admit a realisation as generalised quantum circuits in which the order between the operations is classically controlled, known as "quantum circuits with classical control of causal order".
summary: This theoretical paper characterizes multipartite causal separability in quantum processes, showing that the abstract mathematical condition is equivalent to the physical realization as a quantum circuit with classical control over the order of operations. By developing a novel 'coherent teleportation technique,' the authors complete the characterization, providing a powerful tool for understanding causality in quantum information theory.
main_problem: The paper aims to provide a complete characterization of causal separability in general multipartite quantum processes.
main_result: They prove that a quantum process is causally separable if and only if it can be realized as a quantum circuit where the order of operations is controlled classically (QC-CCs).
method: The authors utilize a novel "coherent teleportation technique" within the process matrix framework to establish the necessity of previously known sufficient conditions.
model_or_system: The study analyzes multipartite quantum processes described by process matrices $W \in \mathcal{A}^{N}_{IO}$, which encode correlations between $N$ parties performing local quantum operations.
key_observables: The process matrix $W$ and the constraint equations derived from the causal separability definition (e.g., Eq. (9)).
important_parameters: The number of parties $N$, and the structure of the local quantum operations (CP maps $M_{A_kIO}^{a_k|x_k}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the process matrix framework and the recursive definition of causal separability.
paper_structure: The paper reviews the process matrix framework and causal separability, then employs the coherent teleportation technique to prove that the necessary condition for causal separability is equivalent to the process admitting a QC-CC realization.
why_interesting: This work provides a fundamental structural characterization of quantum correlations based on causality, which is crucial for understanding the limits of quantum computation and communication protocols.
